articleSummary: Mathematical modeling published July 2026 in Nature Human Behaviour argues smallpox arrived in Australia with the British First Fleet, not from Makassar. articleHeadline: Indian scientists may have found a way to stop malaria
articleSummary: Ark1, or Aurora-related Kinase 1, identified by Indian and British researchers as a key regulator of Plasmodium cell division, offers a potential route to stop malaria. The discovery emerged from India (Pune, Delhi) and the UK (University of Nottingham) collaborations, employing Ultra Expansion Microscopy to visualize Ark1's role despite Plasmodium's microscopic size. The teams plan to map the broader network of Ark1-controlled proteins to understand parasite biology and coordinate drug targeting. With rising chloroquine and artemisinin resistance, Ark1 and related protein kinases are promising druggable targets for novel anti-malarials, aiming to block parasite multiplication in both human erythrocytes and the mosquito vector.
